prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / style-transfer.
Image 1 is the EVA engineering exosuit to edit. Images 2 and 3 are the project's cargo loading hatch and exterior cargo box, authoritative PAINTING STYLE references only.
User request: Match the cargo assets' treatment of surfaces, edges and lighting, but retain the EVA's richer functional detail because players will watch this unit closely. The last over-simplified iteration was rejected. Do NOT simplify the silhouette or erase functional details.
Change ONLY surface rendering and bevel treatment in image 1. Preserve composition, orientation, full silhouette, square canvas, relative proportions, positions, all arms, circular elbow joints, two independent claw jaws, two tool apertures and amber tip, paired cyan nozzles, backpack lid, shoulder panel seams, gray segmented cockpit frame, teal canopy, small yellow lower-body panel and tucked lower appendages.
Study images 2 and 3: large quietly colored panels, fine separation lines, narrow restrained edge highlights and shallow recesses. Their plates read as thin sheet metal, not deeply sculpted faceted armor. Use that SAME visual grammar on the EVA. Allow more joints and panel construction than the cargo box.
Specific corrections:
1. Shoulder yellow armor: main upper plane should extend across almost the entire plate. Replace the current broad gold-brown lower bevel and bright beveled rim with a narrow low-contrast edge, about 2–3 percent of plate width. Keep the existing panel seam and small dark inset, draw them as fine dark lines with at most a subtle narrow highlight, not carved troughs.
2. Gray torso/window surround: preserve the segmented plates and seam layout, but flatten the broad silver/dark polygon gradients. Use quiet neutral gray fields with shallow narrow edge shading like the cargo hatch. No bright silver faceting around the canopy.
3. Claw and tool housing: preserve mechanical construction, replace wide shining bevels with narrow matte edge shading. Articulation must remain readable.
4. Backpack and cuff panels: retain lids and joints, remove wide golden bevel bands, use muted mustard paint and narrow edges.
5. Glass: dark desaturated blue-green with a subdued single reflection, less contrast than before.
Palette stays engineering yellow and neutral gray, not recolored all-gray. Smooth matte broad colors, subtle tonal variation is acceptable like the cargo examples. Thin charcoal internal lines, slightly stronger clean outer outline. No glossy CG lighting, metallic specular shine, sculpted deep bevels, black gutters, new microdetails, extra greebles, labels or decals. No deletion of existing joints/tools. This should be a usable, moderately detailed RimWorld game sprite.
Output ONLY the edited EVA, single isolated complete unit on genuinely transparent background. Do not include cargo assets, comparison panels, text, floor, cast shadow, vignette, smoke or beam effects. Preserve image 1 camera and pose for a direct before/after surface-style comparison.
review: Visual comparison against actual cargo textures: broad shoulder, backpack and cockpit bevel shading reduced; thin panel edges and seams retained, with articulated joints, claw and cutter/welder detail intact. Composition remains the same concept view. Four-direction production assets and actual in-game scale remain pending.
